title: Coast Guard aircraft carrying DHS Secretary Mullin loses engine, lands safely at Reagan National
dek: A 25-year-old Coast Guard twin-engine aircraft carrying Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin lost its right engine on Wednesday afternoon and made an emergency landing at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport. All 14 people aboard, including the secretary, were unharmed.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: The pilot declared an emergency around 1:35 p.m. ET, reporting engine loss and requesting immediate landing with 2.5 hours of fuel remaining; the plane landed safely with no injuries or operational disruptions.
bottom_line: A formal investigation into the engine failure and the aircraft's maintenance records will determine whether this was an isolated mechanical anomaly or evidence of a broader maintenance or inspection gap in the government aircraft fleet.
body:
A Coast Guard plane carrying Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin made an emergency landing at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport on Wednesday afternoon after losing its right engine, according to NBC News and ABC News. All 14 people aboard, including the secretary, were unharmed.
The pilot declared an emergency around 1:35 p.m. ET, stating "we just lost our right engine and would like to declare an emergency and an immediate landing at DCA," according to NBC News. The pilot reported 14 people on board and approximately 2.5 hours of fuel remaining.
The aircraft, a 25-year-old twin-engine plane, landed safely and was thoroughly checked by Airports Authority Fire and Rescue personnel before proceeding off the runway with no disruption to other flights, according to the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority, per NBC News. No injuries were reported.
Multin posted on X following the landing: "The United States Coast Guard pilots made the single engine landing feel routine. No panic, just straight professionalism. After we landed, the pilots told me that was a first for them! We could not have been in better hands."
